classification.difficultyReason: Standardise, find a two-tailed probability by doubling a tail, and compare it with 0.05 to reach a yes/no judgement. The definition of unusual is supplied, so the interpretation is scaffolded.

content.prompt: Loaf masses from a bakery are normally distributed with a mean of 750 g and standard deviation of 12 g. A loaf is unusual if the probability of a loaf being at least as far from the mean, in either direction, is less than 0.05. Is a 730 g loaf unusual? Use the standard normal distribution table. Round calculated z-scores to 2 decimal places and give probabilities to 4 decimal places.

answer.short: No. The probability is $0.0950$, which is not less than $0.05$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}z&=\frac{730-750}{12}\\z&=-\frac53\\z&\approx-1.67\end{aligned}$$
By symmetry,
$$\begin{aligned}P(Z\le-1.67)&=1-P(Z\le1.67)\\&=1-0.9525\\&=0.0475\end{aligned}$$
Both directions count, so
$$\begin{aligned}P(|Z|\ge1.67)&=2\times0.0475\\&=0.0950\end{aligned}$$
Since $0.0950>0.05$, a 730 g loaf is not unusual.
